assets: the tower/gate verdict on a commit, the only proof the merge queue takes
the gate's rules, scripts and workflows
boundaries: a pull request's code (a session's, or a fork's) and the GitHub-hosted runner that judges it
the pull request run and the merge queue run that reuses its tests' verdict
the staged workflows of this tree and the ones the owner installs in .github/workflows

threats.statement: A run that did not judge the commit, such as a fork's run or a run of another head, passes its green verdict off as the queue commit's; or a tower/gate status is posted on a commit by a credential other than the gate's own job. The ruleset binds each required check to the GitHub Actions app (integration 15368), so a status of that name from a session's credential (verify-commit without --no-post) or any other writer does not count. Residual: the binding names the GitHub Actions app, not the workflow, so a change that edits the workflow defines its own check; GitHub refuses such a push without the workflow scope, which only the owner holds here (D-087), but a fork's pull request carries its own workflow (VULN-gate-check-source is fixed: the owner applied the binding on 19/11).

A pull request edits the gate itself (its scripts, its rules, its registry keys, the verifier or a workflow) so that its own change passes. The gate's files (GATE_FILE: the stages, the structure and commit checks, config/registry/gate/, scripts/verify-commit) ask a decision, and the pinned job of tower/gate judges a change to them with the base's gate: the base's gate_pin.py puts the base's gate files back in the checkout and the plan's stages run there (D-070 on GitHub). The overlay covers the gate files of GATE_FILE; their import closure in scripts/lib (static ast and heredoc imports, a module name built from a literal start); the top-level scripts and files the base's stage commands run or read by path (scripts/gate-check's "$root/scripts/generate" and scripts/schema-compat, "$(dirname "$0")/lib/x.py", ROOT / 'scripts' / 'x', .gitleaks.toml) with their own closure; the toolchain (TOOLCHAIN_FILE); and every registry owner whose key the closure's code reads (config.get literals, ou_config_value) when the change alters that key (VULN-gate-judged-by-own-head, fixed). Residual: the workflow itself is the owner's to change (D-087), and the head's tests run the head's code, as code under test.

A dependency or tool the gate runs is swapped for a malicious version between two runs. Residual: the workflows' actions are pinned by commit today, but no check refuses a tag pin; the supply measure counts one as unpinned.
A pushed history is rewritten so that what merged is not what was judged.
A merge cannot be traced to the verdict and the commit that justified it.

A secret committed in a change reaches the public repository and its history. Residual: the gate sees a pushed commit, already public on its branch; the earlier barrier is the pre-push scan, which runs on the client and is skipped by a push that bypasses the hook.

A change floods the queue or hangs the gate, so no other change lands. Residual: the 60 s requirement is a target, not a bound; a hung run is stopped by the job's timeout and the queue's check timeout.

The ruleset requires no approving review (D-055), so any account that may push a branch and enqueue it lands whatever passes the gate's checks; the checks, not a person, are the whole barrier. Residual: a change that is malicious but passes every rule is not caught.

findings.finding: The ruleset (.github/rulesets/main.json) requires tower/gate, web and gate pinned to the base with integration_id 15368 (GitHub Actions), and security.test.sh refuses a required check that names no source app. VULN-gate-check-source records that the owner applied it to the live ruleset on 19/11.
findings.reason: holds in the files; the live ruleset was not read by this review (no network), the VULN record is the evidence. The threat's residual still said the binding was only staged; corrected in its text.

findings.finding: A pull request that edits .github/workflows/tower-gate.yml (or adds a job named tower/gate or gate pinned to the base to another allowed workflow) defines its own check: pull_request and merge_group runs take the workflow file from the commit under judgment, and every repository-side check (gate_workflows.refused, queue-checks' installed == staged, the structure and commit-check rules, the pinned job) runs inside that workflow, so the change can remove them. The ruleset's app binding names GitHub Actions, not a workflow. GitHub's server-side refusal of a push that touches .github/workflows without the workflow scope is a real barrier for this repository's own branches, since sessions hold no such token (D-087), and the owner's own change is an accepted residual. It does not cover a fork: its author holds that scope on the fork, the fork's workflow runs on the pull request and enters the merge group commit, and the only barrier left is that someone with write access enqueues it (required_approving_review_count 0, D-055).
findings.reason: the owner path is an accepted residual (D-087), the fork path is not mitigated: needs a repository-side rule on .github/** (for example a ruleset or code-owner review required for changes there, or fork pull request workflows kept from the queue), or an owner's recorded acceptance of the fork path.

findings.finding: The job pinned is installed: .github/workflows/tower-gate.yml equals the staged services/runner/github/tower-gate.yml, runs the base's gate_pin.py overlay from a worktree of the base and verify-commit --stages-only, and tower/gate needs it green; the ruleset also requires it by name.
findings.reason: verified in the files; VULN-gate-judged-by-own-head is recorded fixed.

findings.finding: The overlay's earlier gaps: (a) gate_closure restores the import closure of GATE_FILE (test_gate_pin proves every structure.py import is in it); (b) TOOLCHAIN_FILE covers scripts/cloud, the hermetic harness and .toolchain, and the pinned job restores no cache, so setup.sh, env.sh and python3 are the base's; (c) scripts/verify-commit and verify_commit.py are GATE_FILE, so a change to the verifier that chooses the parts' tests asks a decision that the base's pr metadata stage judges.
findings.reason: holds in gate_pin.py and the workflow. (c) remains a decision, not a pin: the parts still run the head's verifier, accepted as the threat's residual (code under test).

findings.finding: The exception regime: regime.exception_active is false (D-340) and GATE_FILE now matches scripts/lib/regime.py and config/registry/regime/, so a change to the regime keys asks a decision and is judged by the base's gate.
findings.reason: verified in config/registry/regime/ and gate_pin.GATE_FILE; the change-store path below is a separate open finding.

findings.finding: Missing threat: The registry's effective value is the latest change in the file store, and the gate reads that store from the checkout it judges (OU_CONFIG_STORE=file; config.store_dir .tower/config, so .tower/config/<repo>/repository.jsonl). The path is gitignored (/.tower/), but `git add -f` tracks it, and nothing refuses a tracked file there; the overlay of the pinned job restores registry files, not that store. Reproduced in a scratch copy: config.set_value('regime.exception_active', true) wrote that file and config.get then returned true. So a pull request that commits a config.changed line can turn the exception regime on (every structure and commit-plan lock warns), loosen a budget or threshold that threshold_check judges only by registry default, or change any gate.* key, with no GATE_FILE change, no decision and no pinning.
findings.reason: Fixed 2026-11-19 in three layers: the structure check's hygiene refuses any tracked path under .tower/ (repo_hygiene.tower_store_errors, STD-repo-hygiene-tower-store-errors, test_repo_hygiene.TowerStore); verify-commit sets OU_CONFIG_REGISTRY_ONLY to its checkout, so every stage and test it runs reads registry defaults only (test_config_api.GateMode, test_verify_commit.GateMode); the pinned overlay deletes .tower/ from the checkout (gate_pin.remove_store, test_gate_pin.Overlay). VULN-gate-tower-config-override.

findings.finding: Supply chain: every action of the installed workflows (checkout, cache, upload-artifact, setup-node) is now pinned by commit, so the residual's 'pinned by a tag' was out of date; corrected in its text. No check refuses a future tag pin; the supply measure counts it.
findings.reason: a workflow change is the owner's (D-087) and the actions are GitHub's own, the party that already runs the runner and the ruleset.

findings.finding: History rewrite: the ruleset's deletion and non_fast_forward rules and the merge queue (merge method MERGE only) refuse it on main; commit-check refuses a force push on the head ref.
The merge commit and the required Actions check run on it trace the verdict; verdict artifacts expire in 7 days and run logs on GitHub's retention.
findings.reason: the merge commit and its required check are the durable record; the logs are supporting evidence.

findings.finding: The secret scans run as gate stages; the residual (the commit is already public on its branch when judged, the pre-push scan is client-side and skippable) is honest.
findings.reason: a pushed branch of a public repository is public before any server-side check can run; the earlier 'fixed' named a residual, so it is recorded as accepted.

findings.finding: Each job has timeout-minutes (30, 30, 5), the queue's check_response_timeout_minutes is 20, and concurrency cancels a superseded run of the same pull request.

No approving review is required, so the checks are the whole barrier. With the regime off the locks refuse again, but the two open findings above (the workflow a fork defines, the tracked change store) let a change get past the checks.
findings.reason: the residual is honest as written (D-055); its strength depends on the two open findings.
